top_violation_types.title: Activities for Infants - Not in Restrictive Device for more than 15 Minutes (26 TAC §746.2417(2)(B))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Children are left in buggies longer than fiftteen minutes which is the maximum time frame a child may be in a restrictive device.

top_violation_types.title: Requirements for Feeding Infants - Other Use of Handwashing Sink (26 TAC §746.2419(8))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The hand washing sink in the infant classroom was observed being used to clean pacifiers as well as prepare bottles.

top_violation_types.title: Supervision ensures each child?s safety, well-being, including physical proximity and auditory or visual awareness of each child?s on going activity (26 TAC §746.1205(a)(4))
AP Background check results - Must receive notification prior to allowing subject to be present at your operation (26 TAC §745.641)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: The operation knowingly allowed persons to be present at the operation before receiving notification from the CBCU that the persons eligibility determination is Eligible, Provisional or Eligible with Conditions.

top_violation_types.title: Responsibilities of Caregivers - Supervision of Children (26 TAC §746.1203(4))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Based on the information gathered during the investigation, it has been determined that a child was left unattended, the caregiver was not at a physical proximity that allowed visual and/or auditory awareness of the child in care.

top_violation_types.title: HRC42.052(d) - Illegal Operation - Not Registered (26 TAC §HRC42.052(d) - Illegal Operation - Not R)
top_violation_types.typical_finding: There were 5 unrelated children found in care at the time of inspection.

top_violation_types.title: Child/Caregiver Ratio - 18 Months Difference in Age (26 TAC §746.1605(1))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Infants were mixed with children greater than 18 months older than they are.

top_violation_types.title: Director's Absence -  Employees Know Who Is in Charge (26 TAC §746.1013(c))
top_violation_types.typical_finding: Employees did not know who was in charge while director was absent. This was corrected during the inspection when director arrived and informed who was in charge.
